column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/helm-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran
# cargo-auto-release. The run reported SUCCESS: `bump` bumped, tagged and
# pushed; `ship` was SKIPPED; the crate was never published; nothing said so.
# The condition was `needs.bump.outputs.bumped == 'true' && !github.event.
# repository.private`, which is correct and deliberate — publishing from a
# private repo leaks code to crates.io and undoes yanks. The failure was that
# nobody had written down which jobs must run for a given input, so a
# deliberate no-publish and a broken no-publish were the same green tick.
# WHAT CHANGED HERE, 2026-08-17 — read this before trusting an older copy of
# these rows. Until that date this workflow had NO privacy guard at all: both
# of its `github.event.repository.private` references were in `runs-on:`
# (runner routing, gates nothing), so `ship` pushed a PRIVATE caller's chart
# to the OCI registry exactly as it pushed a public one. The header used to
# record that as a deliberate tripwire — rows 1 and 2 differed only in a key
# no condition read — and predicted that "the day someone copies
# cargo-auto-release's guard onto `ship`, row 2 turns NOT-RUN". That day is
# this change. Row 2 was not merely re-contexted; it was INVERTED, and the
# tripwire fired exactly as written.
# THE RISK THIS WORKFLOW ACTUALLY CARRIES, stated so nobody rounds it either
# way. `helm package` tars templates/, values.yaml and Chart.yaml — repo
# source — and `ship` pushes that tarball to an OCI registry. So this is a
# real DISCLOSURE case, not the git-tag-only shape (a Go module proxy cannot
# fetch a private repo, so that shape leaks nothing and the guard there would
# be consistency alone). The one over-claim to avoid: a GHCR package can be
# deleted, unlike a crates.io release; what deletion does not recall is
# whatever was already pulled, cached or mirrored.
# AND WHY THE GUARD DID NOT LAND ALONE. Adding `&& !private` by itself would
# have converted every private caller to the graphql-synthesizer failure —
# bumped, tagged, published nothing, green. `publish-withheld` runs in exactly
# the guard's withholding case and prints the sentence a skipped job cannot.
# Rows 2 and 3 are the pair that keeps it honest: the guard must withhold
# WITH a notice, and the opt-in must actually publish. If either row ever
# needs weakening, the change is wrong, not the row.
# TABLE RULES that make these rows verbose on purpose:
#   - every context path any condition touches must be declared in EVERY case;
#     an undeclared path is an ERROR, not an empty default, so an incomplete
#     case can never become a confident verdict. `inputs.publish-from-private`
#     and `always()` are therefore on every row, including rows where neither
#     changes the outcome;
#   - an EMPTY value (needs.bump.outputs.bumped=) models a SKIPPED upstream
#     job, which is a distinct state from 'false';
#   - `ship` needs `bump` and does not call always(), so a skipped `bump`
#     propagates to a skipped `ship` — row 6 pins that. `publish-withheld`
#     DOES call always(), which lifts it out of that rule, so its skip in
#     row 6 has to come from its own condition and not from needs-propagation.
# NOT ASSERTED, because it is outside what job selection can see: this table
# proves `ship` is SELECTED, never that the chart became resolvable. That is
# the job's own final step ("verify the published chart is resolvable"), which
# runs inside `ship` and is a different layer of check. Likewise it proves
# `publish-withheld` is selected, not that anyone reads the notice it prints.
# 1. The healthy public release. Both release jobs run; the withheld notice
# stays quiet, which is the only case where silence is the correct output.
public-bump
# 2. THE ROW THE WHOLE CHANGE IS FOR. A private caller bumped and did not opt
# in: `ship` must stand down AND `publish-withheld` must run. Asserting only
# the skip would have re-created the silent-skip defect and called it fixed —
# the RAN half of this row is what makes the skip a statement.
private-bump-withheld
# 3. The escape hatch, asserted rather than assumed: a private source that
# deliberately produces a public chart sets publish-from-private=true and
# publishes, with no withheld notice contradicting it. Without this row the
# input could be silently inert and every case above would still pass.
private-bump-opt-in
# 4. Nothing under source-paths changed, so helm-bump reports bumped=false and
# `ship` must skip. A no-op run is a legitimate green, and this row is what
# distinguishes it from a broken one. `publish-withheld` must ALSO stay quiet:
# nothing was withheld, because nothing was ready to publish.
public-no-bump
# 5. Same no-bump outcome from a private caller. The skip is driven by the bump
# result, not by visibility — and crucially the notice does not fire either,
# so a private repo with nothing to release does not get told a publish was
# withheld. A notice on every quiet run is how a notice stops being read.
private-no-bump
# 6. The loop guard. `bump` pushes a commit as the bot, and that push re-enters
# this workflow; `if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'` stops the second
# pass. `bump` is skipped, so `bumped` is EMPTY (not 'false'). `ship` is
# skipped by needs-propagation; `publish-withheld` calls always() so
# needs-propagation cannot skip it — its skip comes from `bumped != 'true'`
# alone. That is the row that catches a future edit loosening its condition
# into a notice on every bot push.
bot-actor-no-loop
# 7. The payload-absent state: `github.event.repository.private` resolves to
# nothing, so `!private` is TRUE and the guard falls OPEN — the chart
# publishes and no notice fires. This row models the STATE, and deliberately
# does not claim which events produce it; the runner-routing comment in the
# workflow says scheduled callers "may" lack github.event.repository, and that
# hedge is not upgraded here. Pinned because a reader of rows 2 and 3 would
# otherwise conclude a private repo can never publish without the opt-in.
absent-repository-payload
